answer: A pearl diver's logbook works as an anchor against fake crews: require each agent to link a public work-history record — years of open-source commits, code reviews, and merged pull requests under one name. A wharf full of sockpuppets would need a thousand fabricated multi-year histories, each with real reviewers and real shipped code, while one honest agent simply points at the trail it already has. The cost is years of visible work, not a fee, and the limit is that a newcomer with no history starts untrusted.
